invariants.name: generated codes are collision-free under concurrency
invariants.oracle: generate_project_code and generate_change_order_number are collision-free under concurrency - two creations at the same instant produce two codes, proven by racing them

invariants.name: original + approved COs = current budget
invariants.oracle: original budget plus the sum of approved change orders equals the current budget - a change order that moves the budget without a ledger row is the one-sided-write class

invariants.name: an approved change order is frozen
invariants.oracle: an approved change order cannot be re-approved or edited - terminal state frozen, proven by attempting the transition

invariants.name: project_links cannot cross a tenant
invariants.oracle: every linked object across all six domains resolves in the project's own hive

invariants.name: list and detail progress cannot disagree
invariants.oracle: progress % on the list and the detail derive from the same v_project_progress_truth row and cannot disagree

invariants.name: archiving leaves no orphans
invariants.oracle: deleting or archiving a project leaves no orphan item, link, role, progress log or change order

domain_truths.name: progress % states its basis
domain_truths.oracle: progress % states its basis - weighted by cost, item count, or planned hours; a bare % is a claim nobody can check

domain_truths.name: budget carries currency and VAT treatment
domain_truths.oracle: budget figures carry their currency and whether they include VAT

domain_truths.name: planned/committed/actual are three labelled numbers
domain_truths.oracle: planned, committed and actual are three distinct numbers, each labelled; none renders in another's place

domain_truths.name: a change order states budget AND schedule effect
domain_truths.oracle: a change order states its effect on both budget and schedule - a cost-only change order hides half its consequence

domain_truths.name: an on-track parent has no overdue child
domain_truths.oracle: an item shown on-track cannot have an overdue child item; the rollup respects its children

domain_truths.name: who may approve is stated; the approver is named
domain_truths.oracle: who may approve a change order is stated on the surface, and the approver is named on the approved row

domain_truths.name: linked evidence counts once
domain_truths.oracle: the same logbook entry linked twice is one piece of evidence, not two

domain_truths.name: the displayed code equals the stored code
domain_truths.oracle: the project code displayed equals the code stored, and its format is stable per hive
